tools.name: lint_music
tools.title: Check the music
tools.description: Static analysis of the notes, as a reviewer listens: notes ringing into a chord change whose chord does not hold them (an error when a semitone against it), notes held under a chord a semitone from its tones, the same pitch written twice at once on a track, notes outside the key and the chord (info), notes an instrument cannot play (Chorda A0–C8, a kit's missing pads). Give the chart for the harmony checks; without it, doubling, key and range only. Each finding: severity, message, track, clip, note id, position. Changes nothing.

chart.description: The chords. Text in bars: bars split by |, the chords of a bar by spaces sharing it equally, "." holds the chord before for one more share, "%" repeats the bar before, "N.C." is no chord — "Fm9 | Dbmaj7 | Abadd9 | Eb Eb/G" (4 bars; the last two beats each in 4/4), "C . . G7" (C for three beats, G7 for one). Symbols: C, Cm, C7, Cmaj7 (CM7, CΔ), Cm7, Cm7b5 (Cø), Cdim7, Caug, Csus2, Csus4, C7sus4, C6, C6/9, Cadd9, C9, Cm9, Cmaj9, C11, C13, C7b9, C7#9, C7#11, C7alt, C5, slash basses (Eb/G). Or a list of {"at", "chord", "length"} with positions.

at.description: Where the chord starts — a position: beats (quarter notes) from the song's start as a number, or "bar:beat" text with bar and beat from 1 ("9:1", "9:2.5"; the beat is the metre's).

length.description: How long (left out: to the next chord; required for the last) — a length: beats (quarter notes) as a number, or "N bars" / "N beats" text.

chart_start_bar.description: The bar the text chart's first bar is (ignored for a list).

track_ids.description: The tracks to check (left out: every track with notes).

from.description: Check notes from here — a position: beats (quarter notes) from the song's start as a number, or "bar:beat" text with bar and beat from 1 ("9:1", "9:2.5"; the beat is the metre's).

to.description: …to here — a position: beats (quarter notes) from the song's start as a number, or "bar:beat" text with bar and beat from 1 ("9:1", "9:2.5"; the beat is the metre's).

key.description: The key to check against (left out: the project's key, if it has one).

scale.description: major, minor, dorian, mixolydian, harmonic_minor… (set_song's list).

info.description: Include notes outside the key (info), not only warnings and errors.

tools.name: separate_stems
tools.title: Separate stems
tools.description: Separate audio into its parts with a model that runs on this computer: HT-Demucs splits a song into drums, bass, other and vocals (model "htdemucs"), or adds guitar and piano ("htdemucs-6s", whose piano is weak). Give a track (every audio clip on it) or audio clips, all on one track and in the arrangement (clips on several tracks, or session clips, are refused: separate one track at a time). The parts land as new audio tracks right under the track, on a new mixer bus in a group named after the track, each clip on the same spot as the clip it came from, sample for sample, with its fades, crossfades, comp seams and mute; the part strips and the bus start above 0 dB (+3.01 dB each under the -3 dB pan law) so the parts sum to the original's level under the project's pan law, and changing the pan law later trims them again; the original clips are muted, not deleted — one undo step. Each new file records the model, its version and licence. Quality "fast" takes about a third of real time on a laptop processor; "best" averages four passes (four times slower, a little cleaner). The model must already be installed (Settings > Models: its licence is the user's to accept); if not, this answers with an error saying so. A long job: it answers with a job handle (wait_job).

tools.name: audio_to_midi
tools.title: Convert audio to MIDI
tools.description: Transcribe an audio clip into notes on a new instrument track under the clip's track, in a MIDI clip aligned to the audio clip (one undo step). Modes: "melody" (one line, for a voice or a solo instrument), "polyphonic" (every note, chords included; Spotify's Basic Pitch) and "drums" (kick, snare, toms, hi-hat, cymbals on General MIDI keys, played by Pulsus). Only the arrangement's audio clips are converted: a session clip is refused (it has no place on the timeline for the MIDI clip to line up with). Notes keep the timing they were played with unless `quantize` is given. Drums are reliable for kick, snare and hi-hat; toms and cymbals are written by default only when the drum model is installed.
